title: Bounded ambient base change for integral stratum extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all arrows are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. On their small pro-étale sites put $R_V=\mathcal O_{E,V}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use module pullback and its composition maps [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], applied termwise to bounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and open extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek].

Let $h:T'\to T$, let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be open with closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$, and form their fibre products $j':U'\hookrightarrow T'$ and $i':Z'\hookrightarrow T'$, with projections $h_U:U'\to U$ and $h_Z:Z'\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $N\in D^b(U,R_U)$ the map
$$\beta_N:j'_!h_U^*N\longrightarrow h^*j_!N$$
adjoint to $h_U^*N\cong j'^*h^*j_!N$, using the open adjunction unit and pullback composition, is an isomorphism. For every $N\in D^b(Z,R_Z)$ the map
$$\gamma_N:h^*i_*N\longrightarrow i'_*h_Z^*N$$
is an isomorphism; it is the closed adjunction unit followed by $i'^*h^*i_*N\cong h_Z^*N$. Under the canonical identifications, $j'^*\beta_N$ and $i'^*\gamma_N$ are identities, while $i'^*\beta_N$ and $j'^*\gamma_N$ are the maps between zero objects.

Consequently, for a locally closed immersion factored as $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow\overline S\hookrightarrow T$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed, put $a_!=i_*u_!$. For its base change $a'=i'\circ u'$ and projection $h_S:S\times_TT'\to S$, the composite of $\gamma^{-1}$ and $\beta$ gives a natural isomorphism
$$a'_!h_S^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*a_!M\qquad(M\in D^b(S,R_S)).$$
No constructibility or derived-completeness hypothesis is imposed on these bounded inputs.

proof.text: Check the geometric hypotheses for every complementary pair used below, including the pair inside $\overline S$. A finite-type $k$-scheme has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. Apply the finite-type Noetherian-spectrum lemma with $R=k$ (whose spectrum is a point). An ascending chain of opens stabilizes on each member of the finite cover, hence stabilizes globally. Every open is quasi-compact: otherwise, successively choosing members of an open cover not contained in the preceding finite union produces a strictly ascending chain. The same applies to its intersection with any affine open, so each open immersion in question is quasi-compact. Base change preserves the open and closed immersion hypotheses by the two cited permanence lemmas. Their ranges remain complementary: by the base-change image lemma (with $C$ the whole source) the range of $j'$ is $h^{-1}(j(U))$ and the range of $i'$ is $h^{-1}(i(Z))$, and these preimages of complementary subsets of $T$ are complementary in $T'$; the same holds for $u'$ and the complement of its range in $\overline S\times_TT'$. Thus the retrocompact-complement hypothesis of Tag 09BM and the quasi-compact-open hypothesis of Tag 09AH hold on both bases.

proof.text: Use the Cartesian-coefficient theorem with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$: every pullback is exact and its underlying functor is inverse image, with the action transferred along $\alpha_f^{-1}$. Apply the internal-module-operations transport equivalences to identify the actual internal pullback/direct-image and open adjunctions with the section-ring ones, including units and counits. The ringed open-closed theorem, applied to $B_T$ and its inverse-image coefficient rings, supplies exact $j_!,i_*$, isomorphisms $j^{-1}j_!\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $i^{-1}i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$, both mixed zero restrictions, and the short exact sequence whose arrows are the actual counit and unit. Those two isomorphisms are not stated to be the adjunction maps; the actual open unit and closed counit are invertible because of the sequence: applying the exact $i^{-1}$ to it and using $i^{-1}j_!=0$, the map $i^{-1}$ of the unit at $M$ is invertible, so by the triangle identity the counit is invertible at every $i^{-1}M$, hence at every module $N\cong i^{-1}i_*N$ by naturality; dually, applying $j^{-1}$ and $j^{-1}i_*=0$ makes $j^{-1}$ of the counit invertible, so the unit is invertible at every $j^{-1}M$, hence at every $N\cong j^{-1}j_!N$. The ring isomorphisms $i^{-1}B_T\cong B_Z$ and $j^{-1}B_T\cong B_U$ of the transport theorem identify module categories over the inverse-image rings with $\operatorname{Mod}(B_Z)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}(B_U)$, and under them $i^{-1},j^{-1}$ are the sectionwise pullbacks. Transfer that sequence and those properties back through the exact equivalences. No finite or discrete coefficient hypothesis is used: the ringed theorem permits an arbitrary sheaf of commutative rings.

proof.text: Apply exact open-closed unbounded calculus with $(J,P,Q,I)=(j_!,j^*,i^*,i_*)$, and again for the primed pair. Its hypotheses are precisely the exactness, adjunctions, units/counits, mixed vanishings and short exact sequence verified in step 2. Thus the actual derived adjunctions have invertible open units $\eta_j,\eta_{j'}$ and closed counits $\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_{i'}$, the mixed restrictions vanish, and $(j'^*,i'^*)$ jointly reflects isomorphisms. The exact-functor cohomology theorem gives $H^q(FK)\cong F(H^qK)$ for every functor here and for $h^*,h_U^*,h_Z^*$, so these functors preserve both cohomological bounds. All subsequent constructions therefore restrict to the ordinary bounded categories in the statement.

proof.text:
The pullback-composition isomorphisms give $c_U:j'^*h^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_U^*j^*$ and $c_Z:i'^*h^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_Z^*i^*$. Use exact-derived composition and natural-isomorphism descent to take these very comparisons termwise to derived categories. Fix $\beta_N$ by transposing
$$t_N=c_{U,j_!N}^{-1}\circ h_U^*(\eta_{j,N}):h_U^*N\longrightarrow j'^*h^*j_!N.$$
Fix $\gamma_N$ as
$$h^*i_*N\xrightarrow{\eta_{i',h^*i_*N}}i'_*i'^*h^*i_*N\xrightarrow{i'_*(h_Z^*(\varepsilon_{i,N})\circ c_{Z,i_*N})}i'_*h_Z^*N.$$
These are exactly the maps of the statement, since the adjunctions in step 3 localize the actual sheaf units/counits. Naturality follows from the naturality of the units, counits and $c_U,c_Z$, or by transposing each naturality square. This defines maps on all bounded inputs, before imposing any support or constructibility condition.

proof.text:
The open adjunction formula gives
$$j'^*(\beta_N)\circ\eta_{j',h_U^*N}=t_N.$$
Both the unit on the left and $t_N$ are invertible, so $j'^*\beta_N$ is invertible. Identifying its source with $h_U^*N$ by $\eta_{j'}$ and its target with $h_U^*N$ by $h_U^*(\eta_j^{-1})\circ c_U$, the displayed equality says its restriction is the identity. On the closed part, $i'^*j'_!h_U^*N=0$, while $i'^*h^*j_!N\cong h_Z^*i^*j_!N=0$ by $c_Z$ and the mixed vanishing. Thus $i'^*\beta_N$ is the unique map between zero objects and is invertible. Joint reflection from step 3 proves that $\beta_N$ itself is invertible.

source.place: Tags 09BN, 09AH; elementary adjunction and complementary-restriction calculation using steps 3--4

proof.text:
The closed adjunction formula, equivalently its triangle identity and counit naturality, gives
$$\varepsilon_{i',h_Z^*N}\circ i'^*(\gamma_N)=h_Z^*(\varepsilon_{i,N})\circ c_{Z,i_*N}.$$
The counit on the left and the whole right side are invertible. Hence $i'^*\gamma_N$ is invertible and, after the indicated counit identifications of both ends with $h_Z^*N$, is the identity. On the open part, $j'^*h^*i_*N\cong h_U^*j^*i_*N=0$ and $j'^*i'_*h_Z^*N=0$. Its open restriction is therefore the unique map between zero objects and is invertible. Joint reflection from step 3 proves that $\gamma_N$ is invertible. This also verifies all four restriction normalizations claimed in the statement.

proof.text:
For $a=i\circ u$, write $h_{\overline S}:\overline S\times_TT'\to\overline S$. Apply step 5 to $u$ inside $\overline S$ and step 6 to $i$, with input $u_!M$. The required composite is explicitly
$$i'_*u'_!h_S^*M\xrightarrow{i'_*(\beta_{u,M})}i'_*h_{\overline S}^*u_!M\xrightarrow{\gamma_{i,u_!M}^{-1}}h^*i_*u_!M.$$
Every factor is an isomorphism and natural in $M$. The fibre-product identifications are those of the given factorization; no independence of the choice of factorization is asserted or needed. Exactness and step 3 keep $u_!M$ and every displayed object bounded. The proof used neither constructibility nor derived completeness, so it applies to every bounded input as stated.
